code.text: Spotting, then light bleeding on and off for about three weeks, eight years after her periods stopped; no pain
She does not want a wait-and-see answer: she knows that bleeding after menopause is sometimes put down to nothing, and she wants the cause found quickly and told plainly
She wants to keep working and to decide who is told
No known allergy

medicationCodeableConcept.text: Acetaminophen 500 mg oral tablet, two tablets by mouth every 6 hours as needed for pain after surgery, no more than 3 g a day

dosageInstruction.text: Two tablets every 6 hours as needed

medicationCodeableConcept.text: Dostarlimab 50 mg/mL injection, 500 mg intravenously over 30 minutes on day 1 of each 21-day cycle, before carboplatin and paclitaxel, for six cycles

dosageInstruction.text: Day 1 every 21 days for six cycles

medicationCodeableConcept.text: Carboplatin 10 mg/mL injection, 575 mg (AUC 5) intravenously on day 1 of each 21-day cycle, for six cycles

dosageInstruction.text: Day 1 every 21 days for six cycles

medicationCodeableConcept.text: Paclitaxel 6 mg/mL injection, 320 mg (175 mg/m2) intravenously over 3 hours on day 1 of each 21-day cycle, for six cycles, after dexamethasone, diphenhydramine and famotidine

dosageInstruction.text: Day 1 every 21 days for six cycles

Levothyroxine 75 mcg oral tablet, one tablet daily before breakfast

code.text: Office endometrial biopsy with a suction catheter (Pipelle), with a chaperone, after verbal consent: adequate tissue obtained; tolerated with mild cramping

Transvaginal ultrasound of the pelvis: endometrium 16 mm, heterogeneous, with an irregular junction with the myometrium and internal blood flow; two small intramural fibroids (1.8 cm and 1.2 cm); ovaries normal for age; no free fluid

coding.display: CT of chest, abdomen and pelvis

code.text: CT of the chest, abdomen and pelvis with contrast: enlarged, heterogeneous uterine cavity; a 1.5 cm right external iliac lymph node and a 1.7 cm left para-aortic lymph node below the renal veins, both suspicious; no liver, lung, bone or peritoneal lesion; no ascites
Advance care planning conversation, about 20 minutes
Screening mammogram, both breasts

coding.display: Laparoscopic total abdominal hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy

code.text: Robotic-assisted total laparoscopic hysterectomy with removal of both fallopian tubes and ovaries and pelvic washings. Pathology: endometrioid adenocarcinoma, FIGO grade 2 (low grade), 4.2 cm, invading 65% of the myometrial thickness; no cervical stromal invasion; focal (not substantial) lymphovascular space invasion; tubes, ovaries and serosa free; washings negative. Mismatch repair deficient (loss of MLH1 and PMS2), MLH1 promoter hypermethylated, POLE wild-type, p53 wild-type; estrogen receptor positive. FIGO 2023 stage IIIC2ii, molecular class MMRd
Sentinel lymph node mapping with indocyanine green, both sides of the pelvis: right external iliac sentinel node with a 9 mm metastasis; left obturator sentinel node negative on ultrastaging
Excision of the enlarged left para-aortic lymph node seen on CT, with adjacent para-aortic nodes below the renal veins: 1 of 4 nodes involved (14 mm deposit)

Genetic counseling: universal Lynch syndrome tumor screening explained; MLH1 and PMS2 loss explained by MLH1 promoter hypermethylation, which is acquired in the tumor and not inherited; germline testing not indicated; she was told what would change that advice

text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Gynecologic oncology consultation within two weeks to review the endometrial biopsy and ultrasound with her and plan treatment if cancer or atypical hyperplasia is found
  • Any bleeding after menopause is evaluated: speculum and bimanual examination, office endometrial biopsy at the first visit, and transvaginal ultrasound within the week, both done rather than relying on endometrial thickness alone; blood count and A1c; results by telephone within days, not at a routine visit
  • Staging and molecular classification: CT of the chest, abdomen and pelvis; mismatch repair immunohistochemistry and p53 on the biopsy, with MLH1 promoter methylation testing for MLH1 loss and POLE sequencing on the surgical specimen; FIGO 2023 stage with the molecular class recorded
  • Robotic-assisted total laparoscopic hysterectomy with removal of both tubes and ovaries, pelvic washings, sentinel lymph node mapping with indocyanine green, and removal of the enlarged pelvic and para-aortic nodes
  • Lynch syndrome screening of the tumor for every endometrial cancer, with genetic counseling; germline testing if mismatch repair loss is not explained by MLH1 promoter methylation, and cascade testing offered to blood relatives only if a germline variant is found
  • Dostarlimab 500 mg with carboplatin (AUC 5) and paclitaxel 175 mg/m2 every three weeks for six cycles, then dostarlimab 1000 mg every six weeks for up to three years, for mismatch repair deficient stage IIIC2 disease; hepatitis B, hepatitis C and HIV screening first; three-drug antiemetic prevention; blood counts, kidney function and magnesium before each cycle; TSH, free T4, liver tests, glucose and morning cortisol at baseline and before each cycle; neuropathy checks at each visit
  • Immune-related hypothyroidism: levothyroxine with TSH and free T4 every six weeks, continuing dostarlimab
  • Survivorship: examination with a pelvic examination every three months for two years, CT of the chest, abdomen and pelvis every six months for three years, no routine vaginal cytology and no CA-125 (normal at diagnosis), teaching on symptoms of recurrence, lymphedema checks, sexual health, weight, activity, blood pressure, lipid and glucose care, distress screening, and age-appropriate screening for other cancers
  • Distress and depression screening at each visit, plain explanations, written information, and support she chooses; she decides who receives each note

resource.title: Gwen Ifill synthetic care plan
resource.description: Evaluate postmenopausal bleeding at once, as any bleeding after menopause requires, in a 60-year-old Black woman, whose risk of dying of endometrial cancer is about twice that of White women because of later diagnosis, more aggressive non-endometrioid and p53-abnormal tumors, and delays in evaluating bleeding: transvaginal ultrasound together with endometrial sampling at the first evaluation (the ACOG update that no longer relies on a thin endometrium alone); histology with the molecular classification (POLE, mismatch repair, p53) that the FIGO 2023 staging uses; CT staging; gynecologic oncology care with minimally invasive hysterectomy and sentinel lymph node mapping; treatment chosen by stage and molecular class, here dostarlimab with carboplatin and paclitaxel for mismatch repair deficient stage IIIC2 disease, with immune-related adverse event monitoring; universal Lynch syndrome tumor screening with MLH1 promoter methylation testing and genetic counseling; and survivorship care, on the NCCN uterine neoplasms guideline, the ACOG postmenopausal bleeding guidance, the SGO surveillance statement and the CMID endometrial cancer monograph.
